controller.policy: incumbent-conditioned diagnostic revision with registered multimodal hypothesis seeds
design_agenda: Instantiate one complete, falsifiable cross-modal perturbation-response hypothesis: encode control profile, chemical representation, and dose separately at a common hidden width; use chemical query with control key/value interaction plus dose residual and layer normalization; pass the fused state through a shared response program; predict the joint response; use CP/L1000 block-aware MSE weighting (0.4/0.6), AdamW, and cosine scheduling. Register chemical-attention use for independent source and behavioral testing.

Instantiate a compact featurewise conditional-fusion alternative: separate modality encoders, chemical-and-dose FiLM or gated modulation of the control program, a residual joint response network, and a block-aware response objective.

Instantiate a response-factorized alternative: modality-specific encoders, a learned cross-modal interaction, shared latent response program, and two block-aware output heads trained jointly without target-wise models.
Test a genuine multi-token cross-modal interaction or low-rank bilinear fusion with explicit dose conditioning; retain only a complete source-local model that respects the joint-output contract.

Test a structured multi-tower response model with residual capacity, normalization, dropout, AdamW, and an objective that balances correlation-sensitive and squared-error response fidelity when justified.
Test whether a compact conditional bottleneck or low-rank joint readout improves the L1000 block without sacrificing the Cell-Painting block; preserve all task semantics.
Using the Fold-3 history, synthesize only mutually compatible mechanisms from earlier attempts into one coherent model and avoid cosmetic rewrites.
Explore one complementary multimodal design that is materially distinct from previous source hashes, with explicit tensor-shape reasoning and registered metadata.
Make one final diagnosis-driven revision of the best incumbent; prioritize a complete, executable perturbation-response hypothesis over a hyperparameter-only change.
